title: Nov 30 2025 - Nova Biotech / Redwood - On‑prem air‑gapped deployment discovery
summary: Discovery for on‑prem, air‑gapped Redwood Private deployment. Customer is regulated (clinical research), requires offline model updates, strict KMS/HSM policy, limited rack space and older GPU fleet; evaluating tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated vs fully air‑gapped Private. Action items: share security pack, hardware worksheet, proposed pilot plan and pricing. Next step: technical deep dive + checklist for procurement.
action_items: Alex Chen (Redwood AE): Share Private deployment security pack and SOC2/ISO artifacts - due 2025-12-06
Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Produce hardware worksheet with supported GPU configs + offline update flow diagram - due 2025-12-04
Ethan Brooks (Nova ML): Send current model sizes, typical seq length and token throughput metrics - due 2025-12-03
next_steps: Schedule SE deep dive for performance/benchmarking (w/ Nova infra team)
Send pricing for 6‑month pilot (dedicated vs private) and pilot success criteria template
Share example offline model bundle signing process and manifest link: https://redwood.example.com/secure/offline-bundles
transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, joining me is Priya our solutions engineer. Quick intro round?
00:12 Dr. Maya Singh (Nova CTO): Hi I'm Maya, CTO at Nova Biotech, we run clinical research pipelines, we need to keep PHI on prem.
00:20 Julian Perez (Infra): Julian here, infra lead, we manage the on prem clusters and procurement for hardware.
:30 Sofia Morales (Security): Sofia, head of security. We'll be focusing on compliance, KMS and air‑gap constraints.
00:45 Alex Chen: Great; objective for today is to understand your constraints — hardware, security and update cadence — and see whether Redwood Hosted/Dedicated or a full Private on‑prem air‑gapped deployment is needed.
01:05 Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Quick note, our Private offering can be deployed in a sealed VPC or completely air‑gapped with offline update tooling. There are a few patterns customers use for model updates: signed bundles via USB or secure physical transfer, and an on‑site HSM for key management.
01:28 Ethan Brooks (ML Eng): We can't expose any PHI offsite. Our current infra is older — mostly A100s from 2021 and some V100s — and we have limited rack space.
01:42 Priya Raman: Okay that matters; A100s are supported, V100s we can run smaller models but buffer and KV cache behave differently. We'll need to map recommended quantization/profiles.
01:58 Sofia Morales: We also need full audit logs, immutable retention for seven years for certain study data, and SSO via our Okta instance.
02:12 Alex Chen: We support SAML/Okta, RBAC, and can integrate with customer KMS or HSM. For air‑gapped installs we typically run a local KMS connector to an on‑prem HSM — gives you control over keys.
02:27 Dr. Maya Singh: How do you handle model updates? We update models quarterly after validation — but in an air gap we need a signed artifact with checksums and a verification chain.
02:40 Priya Raman: We have an offline bundle format: model + runtime metadata + signature. Customers sign with their HSM; Redwood ships a signed verification tool. The update is staged to a test namespace then promoted.
03:02 Julian Perez: Is there any telemetry that leaves the site by default?
03:08 Alex Chen: Default for air‑gapped is zero outbound telemetry. For Private we can enable optional usage metrics pushed via a proxy if you approve, but by default logs stay local.
03:20 Sofia Morales: What about vulnerability patching? In an air‑gapped environment we can't hit public repos.
03:27 Priya Raman: We provide patch bundles and CVE summaries that you can pull into an internal mirror; patch delivery happens via signed bundles and we include reproducible checksums.
03:45 Ethan Brooks: On the performance side, our models are ~8B to 70B, most traffic is batch scoring for research pipelines. Latency is less critical than throughput, but cost is.
03:58 Priya Raman: For batch workloads we recommend Dedicated pools or Private with autoscaling kernels; quantization and batching profiles will reduce token cost. We'll need sample workloads to recommend exact configs.
04:18 Alex Chen: Can you share constraints around storage and network?
04:22 Julian Perez: Storage is limited — about 200TB usable; we can't add extra racks in the near term. Network is internal 25Gbps between nodes.
04:32 Priya Raman: Noted. That affects model sharding and KV cache placement. We can recommend model pruning, off‑node cache or smaller sharded replicas.
05:00 Dr. Maya Singh: Compliance: we need SOC2 type II evidence, but also FDA audit trails for study data. Do you provide immutable audit logs and time‑series of model predictions?
05:14 Alex Chen: We can produce detailed audit logs, immutable append‑only stores, and exportable logs for audits. For FDA traceability we recommend storing model version, prompt/seed, and output hashes in the audit record.
05:33 Sofia Morales: Encryption at rest and in transit? Key rotations?
05:38 Priya Raman: We support AES256 at rest and TLS 1.3 for transit. Key rotation is supported via HSM; for Private installs you control rotation policies.
05:55 Julian Perez: What about hardware compatibility matrix — if we have mixed A100/H100/V100 fleets, does Redwood handle kernel selection?
06:03 Priya Raman: Runtime will select kernels and quantization paths, but older GPUs like V100 may not support optimal kernels for bigger models. We can generate a compatibility sheet — which we'll include in the hardware worksheet.
06:28 Ethan Brooks: We have a procurement window in January, so timeline matters.
06:33 Alex Chen: Good to know. That suggests a pilot in December/January to prove perf and security controls.
06:40 Dr. Maya Singh: What's the fallback if an update fails in air‑gapped mode?
06:46 Priya Raman: We always stage updates to a canary namespace; if health checks fail, the orchestrator rolls back automatically. We also keep a known‑good model bundle to revert to.
07:05 Sofia Morales: Can you describe the offline verification chain again? We need cryptographic guarantees.
07:12 Priya Raman: Bundle is signed using your HSM keys. The bundle contains manifest with checksums for model files and runtime. The on‑site verifier checks signature and verifies checksums before allowing deployment.
07:36 Alex Chen: I'll add a diagram to the follow up showing where signatures happen, the HSM touchpoints and audit log flow.
07:45 Julian Perez: Regarding network isolation, can Redwood run inside our air‑gapped VLANs with no external dependencies?
07:52 Priya Raman: Yes; for fully air‑gapped deployment we provide an installer that doesn't require outbound access. All dependencies are vendored in the bundle.
08:08 Ethan Brooks: Any special licensing for quantized runtimes?
08:13 Alex Chen: No special license beyond the Private package; we do recommend specific quantization profiles which are part of the deployment config.
08:22 Dr. Maya Singh: On the legal side, can we ensure data never leaves premises and that backups are on‑site only?
08:29 Alex Chen: Yes — Private on‑prem can be configured to keep backups on‑site and enforce retention policies.
08:36 Sofia Morales: We need to review your breach notification SLA and to have an SOW clause about handling of incident response for on‑prem installs.
08:45 Alex Chen: We'll include standard SOW language and we can extend SLAs for dedicated/hybrid customers.
09:00 Julian Perez: For benchmarks, do you provide benchmarking harness we can run in our environment?
09:07 Priya Raman: Yes, we provide a portable benchmark harness and sample datasets. For air‑gapped sites, we deliver via signed bundle.
09:18 Ethan Brooks: We might want an initial POC with a 7B model to validate throughput on our A100s.
09:24 Priya Raman: That lines up with our standard pilot: 2 weeks of throughput and accuracy checks. We'll propose success criteria.
09:40 Dr. Maya Singh: Who owns the model artifacts — do we maintain IP?
09:45 Alex Chen: You own the models and data; Redwood manages runtime and deployment per the Private agreement.
09:54 Sofia Morales: What logging does Redwood collect by default during pilot? We need to approve any telemetry.
10:00 Priya Raman: During pilot we can run in full local logging mode; any Redwood access requires your explicit opt‑in and credentials.
10:12 Julian Perez: Procurement asks: pricing for 6‑month pilot and estimates for 1 rack vs 2 racks.
10:19 Alex Chen: We'll send a pilot pricing sheet and a 1‑rack vs 2‑rack cost estimate based on your workload assumptions.
10:30 Dr. Maya Singh: Do you have customers with healthcare regulated on‑prem?
10:35 Alex Chen: Yes, several— we've done air‑gapped installs for clinical research orgs and med devices companies; happy to share redacted references.
10:45 Sofia Morales: Please share any pen test reports and SOC2 reports.
10:49 Alex Chen: We'll attach the security pack with SOC2, pen test summaries and the Private deployment checklist.
11:02 Ethan Brooks: On the model side, will Redwood support sharded attention and KV cache across nodes?
11:10 Priya Raman: Yes, the runtime supports sharded KV and cross‑node attention for large models; for your 70B models, we'll likely need sharding and possibly model parallelism. This ties back to your interconnect and storage.
11:30 Julian Perez: Our internal change window is limited; upgrades need to happen in maintenance windows.
11:35 Priya Raman: Understood — the deployment tooling supports staged rollouts aligned to windows.
11:48 Alex Chen: Recap: Redwood will share security pack, hardware worksheet, offline bundle flow diagram, and a pilot proposal. Nova will share model sizes, throughput samples and procurement timeline.
12:02 Dr. Maya Singh: Sounds good. Let's schedule the SE deep dive next week.
12:08 Alex Chen: I'll send calendar invites and the follow up items. Thanks all.
45:58 Alex Chen: Wrap up. Meeting end.
